There are six compliers, two always-takers and four never-takers. Consistency, no interference, binary receipt, monotonicity D(1) ≥ D(0), exclusion and the known assignment law are separate parts of the identification contract. The binary-compliance result motivates this distinction; the finite population and calculations here are original.

The brief to reproduce and challenge

The fictional draft reports a change contrast of 11/3, first stage 5/6, sample Wald ratio 22/5 and receipt-OLS slope 118/35. Its primary statistic was specified as the change contrast before follow-up measurement. Post-only and baseline-adjusted specifications are disclosed alternatives. It makes four claims: (i) random invitations make course receipt random; (ii) twelve workers justify individual iid uncertainty; (iii) the Wald ratio is finite-sample unbiased and a sharp adjusted-outcome inversion is a generic confidence interval for a heterogeneous complier effect; and (iv) the invitation's randomization proves exclusion. Reproducing the numbers must not silently endorse these claims.

Define the finite encouragement effect θZ = (1/12)Σ[W(D(1),1)−W(D(0),0)], first stage π = (1/12)Σ[D(1)−D(0)], and baseline complier receipt effect θC = (1/6)ΣCτ. Distinguish these from the observed ratio TW/TD, the descriptive OLS coefficient of W on 1,D, and the coefficient of centre W on 1,Z,centred centre B. A change outcome does not itself establish observational parallel trends; this project's assignment law identifies θZ.

Seven required tasks and submission

  1. Reproduce the observed brief. Submit a data dictionary, provenance and execution log, input/output hashes and a discrepancy table. Calculate change ITT, post-only ITT, baseline imbalance, first stage, Wald, receipt OLS, and centre ANCOVA with an intercept. State which records each calculation uses. Refit ANCOVA rather than importing a coefficient from the reference output.
  2. Defend identification and finite expectations. Write a 1,200–1,800 word identification memo defining the targets and assumptions. Derive the finite compliance identity and unbiased assignment contrast. Enumerate the twenty possible assignments using the teaching oracle; compute expectations of both ITTs, the first stage, Wald and ANCOVA. Explain why a ratio of expectations does not equal the expectation of a ratio, and why random assignment does not make receipt OLS causal.
  3. Audit dependence and uncertainty. Prove the finite complete-randomization variance formula and the expected Neyman estimate. Calculate true variance, the realized cluster estimate and the mistaken individual iid estimate. Does “conservative” mean the realized estimate always exceeds true variance? Derive exact two-sided sharp-outcome-null p-values for change ITT and refitted ANCOVA under the actual assignment law. Distinguish these frozen-outcome references from the oracle alternative-law distribution.
  4. Invert a precisely stated null on all of R. Test Hτ: every worker's W(z)−τD(z) is invariant across assignments. Use inclusive ties, reject p ≤ α and retain p > α. Prove the finite-rank size bound and an exact crossing-point algorithm. Find the complete inversion at α = 1/5 and at α = 1/20, including endpoint flags and unbounded tails. State when its coverage claim applies and why it does not provide generic heterogeneous-LATE coverage for these data.
  5. Extension 1: access loss and a zero first stage. Define a separate prospective world in which centre 2 worker 1 changes from C to N, leaving all other primitives fixed, and newly assign centres {1,2,4}. Compute its true assignment effects and CACE, its observed ITT and first stage, the number of undefined assignment ratios and its complete α = 1/5 inversion. Do not edit the original observed evidence or silently drop undefined ratios.
  6. Extension 2: a direct invitation route. For compliers only replace the potential law by Wδ(d,z) = v+(τ−δ)d+δz, for one common δ ∈ [−1,1]. Keep A/N laws and all other primitives fixed. Prove observational equivalence for every allowed assignment, derive the isolated receipt-effect identified set in this class, and give an attainable witness for every point. Explain what the assignment-effect ratio now represents.
  7. Referee judgment and an actual-paper transfer. Submit a concise referee report on the fictional brief and the external-paper dossier specified below. Correct each flawed claim, distinguish matching numbers from valid inference, and give a conditional conclusion. For the external paper, document real access and either execute one bounded reproduction or record an honest limitation. Propose two feasible extensions and a referee report; do not invent numerical external results.

Submit readable independent code and a README, a comparison table, the identification memo, an inference appendix with proofs, the two extension analyses and the two research-audit reports. A 10-minute oral defence asks you to distinguish one estimand from an estimate, trace one null reference, and give one observational-equivalence witness. Word and time budgets are planning aids, not empirical measures of competence.

Mandatory external-paper dossier

Select one actual primary empirical paper with a readable method/results body, a stated target and identifiable data/code provenance. Prefer lawful public data/code and one result small enough to reproduce with available resources. Record the canonical citation and URL, version and access date, exact table/claim/page and what you actually read. Map target population, exposure, estimand, assignment or sampling law, dependence unit, measurement, support and identifying assumptions. A prestigious outlet or successful code run does not establish those assumptions.

Record data/code owners, versions, hashes when acquired, licensing and access restrictions, expected software and the path from inputs to a chosen exhibit. Execution branch: if compatible lawful inputs are available, run that bounded result and retain commands, environment, output, mismatches and any changes. Access-limitation branch: if required inputs or software are unavailable or restricted, record the actual evidence and permitted route inspected, mark “reproduction not executed,” and provide a concrete input/code/claim map and a testable execution protocol. A proposed protocol is not an executed replication. Do not obtain restricted material through workarounds or manufacture output.

In either branch propose two feasible extensions: one changes identification, mechanism or sensitivity; the other examines inference, measurement or support. For each give the needed inputs, changed assumptions, target, diagnostic and decision rule for interpreting the result. The referee report separates major identification/inference/integrity issues from minor presentation issues and states what the available evidence supports. An excellent access audit can earn audit points while the completion record still says external reproduction was not performed. The AEA documentation and access guidance supplies dated professional context, not general law, data permission or certification.

100-point rubric and essential floors

All five domains are essential
DomainPointsFull-credit evidence
Data and reproducibility20Keys/timing/units 4; observed–oracle distinction and assignment law 5; all observed coefficients 7; execution/discrepancy/integrity log 4.
Estimands and identification20Distinct targets 6; complete compliance derivation and assumptions 6; finite estimate/target/bias distinction 4; repaired claims and conditional conclusion 4.
Inference and alternatives20Regressions and refitting 5; finite variance proof 6; separate alternative/null orbits 5; rank, ties, resolution and confidence scope 4.
Extensions and sharpness20Weak-world truth and undefined ratio 5; complete disconnected inversion 5; direct-effect equivalence 6; bounds, witnesses and scope 4.
External transfer and research judgment20Primary scope/access/provenance 4; identification/inference audit 5; actual execution log or evidenced limitation/protocol 4; two feasible extensions 4; referee judgment and honest completion status 3.

Advancement requires 85/100 overall, at least 15/20 in each domain, satisfactory oral transfer and correction of every critical error. These are instructional thresholds, not an institutional credential. Credit valid methods and transparent consequential arithmetic; do not penalize one arithmetic slip repeatedly. An equivalent exact method earns full credit if it preserves the actual assignment law, all ties, undefined estimates and complete interval endpoints.

Critical errors override the score: equating random assignment with random receipt or automatic exclusion; counting workers as independent assignment units; calling this sharp inversion a generic LATE interval; dividing by zero or dropping undefined ratios without conditioning; leaking oracle potential outcomes into observed-data analysis; substituting an unmentioned probability law; selecting a favourable p-value while claiming prespecification; or fabricating access, execution, data rights, empirical replication or source inspection. Remediation requires a corrected calculation, explanation and changed-assignment/direct-effect oral transfer.

Complete instructor guide, derivations and extension answers

1. Reproduce the table and alternative specifications — P2

The centre baseline means are (41,45,49,53,57,61), change means (1,1,11/2,−1,9/2,0) and receipt means (1,0,1,0,1/2,0). Encouraged mean change is 11/3 and unencouraged mean is 0, so TW = 11/3. The baseline contrast is -4, hence post-only ITT is -1/3. This negative post contrast and positive change contrast are not a contradiction: they use different outcomes with an observed baseline imbalance. Both remain design-unbiased for the same encouragement effect because B is fixed before assignment.

The receipt contrast is 5/6, so the sample Wald ratio is 22/5. Among the five recipients, total change is 19; among seven nonrecipients it is 3. OLS on an intercept and binary D is their mean difference, 19/5−3/7 = 118/35. That coefficient is descriptive. Always-takers and compliers select into receipt differently, and fixed untreated changes differ among workers; random Z does not make D independent of potential outcomes.

For centre ANCOVA, put b = B̄−51 = (−10,−6,−2,2,6,10) and X = [1,Z,b]. The exact normal equations are

[[6,3,0],[3,3,−6],[0,−6,280]] β = (11,11,−2)′,
β = (−5/32, 191/48, 5/64)′.

The determinant is positive because Z is not affine in the six distinct baselines; equivalently its residual sum of squares below is positive. For an independent FWL derivation, residualize Z on 1,b: z̃ = Z−1/2+(3/140)b. Then z̃′z̃ = 48/35 and z̃′W̄ = 191/35. Their ratio is the ANCOVA invitation coefficient 191/48. Substituting in the remaining equations gives the intercept and baseline slope. All twenty assignment designs have positive residual rank, which the exact finite computation verifies; no pseudoinverse or “randomization guarantees rank” assertion is needed.

The reproduction log records each transformation and discrepancy. A coefficient copied from a supplied output without a calculation is not replication. The routine for these results needs only observed B,Y,D,Z and group keys. The oracle appears only in the subsequent design audit.

2. Identify assignment effects, then examine estimators — P1 and P2

Write Wzjr = Wjr(Djr(z),z). Exclusion implies W¹−W⁰ = τ[D(1)−D(0)]. Monotonicity and binary receipt make the bracket 1 for C and 0 for A/N. Summing gives π = 6/12 = 1/2, θZ = (2+4+6+2+4+6)/12 = 2 and θC = 4. Thus θZ = πθC. Positive π permits division. Without exclusion, assignment effects can include a direct invitation effect; without monotonicity, positive and negative receipt switches can enter with opposite signs.

At the centre level W̄⁰ = (−2,1,9/2,−1,9/2,0) and W̄¹ = (1,4,11/2,−1,9/2,5). Their differences are (3,3,1,0,0,5), averaging 2. With three treated centres, TW = (1/3)ΣZjW̄¹j−(1/3)Σ(1−Zj)W̄⁰j. Since E[Zj] = 1/2, E[TW] = (1/6)Σ(W̄¹−W̄⁰) = θZ. The identical argument applies to receipt and to post-only outcomes, whose individual encouragement differences equal change differences.

For finite expectations, regenerate D,W,Y under each of the twenty equally likely assignments using the fixed oracle. This is a distribution under the heterogeneous alternative, not a null permutation. Summing each estimated statistic and dividing by twenty gives:

Exact expectations over assignment, not estimates of a superpopulation
StatisticExpectationRelevant finite target
Change ITT; post-only ITT2; 2θZ = 2
First stage1/2π = 1/2
Wald133/40θC = 4 under exclusion
Refitted ANCOVA Z coefficient6057/4160θZ = 2

All baseline first stages lie in [1/6,5/6], so the Wald expectation exists. Its bias is -27/40; ANCOVA's is -2263/4160. The finite table is an exact counterexample to unbiasedness claims, not an argument that adjustment is always worse. The coefficient's random regression denominator and the ratio's random first stage prevent an interchange of expectation with division. The useful identity is E[TW]/E[TD] = 4, not E[TW/TD] = 4.

3. Derive dependence-appropriate uncertainty and exact tests — P3 and P4

For j ≠ k, E[ZjZk] = (3/6)(2/5) = 1/5. Hence Var(Zj) = 1/4 and Cov(Zj,Zk) = −1/20. Let aj = W̄¹j+W̄⁰j. TW differs from (1/3)ΣZjaj only by a constant. Expanding with these covariances gives

Var(TW) = (1/9)[(1/4)Σa² − (1/20)Σj≠kajak] = (1/30)Σ(aj−ā)² = S²a/6 = S²1/3 + S²0/3 − S²effect/6.

Every S² uses denominator 5 across the six centres. The final equality follows from S²sum+S²difference = 2S²1+2S²0. Here S²0 = 23/3, S²1 = 20/3 and S²effect = 4; variance is 37/9. Directly summing (TW−2)²/20 over assignments yields the same value.

For any fixed six numbers x, the sample variance of a uniform three-element subset is unbiased for the population sample variance. To see this, use s² = [1/(3·2)]Σj<k in sample(xj−xk)². Each pair is selected with probability 1/5, and Σj<k(xj−xk)² = 6Σ(x−x̄)². Taking expectation gives (1/30)·6Σ(x−x̄)² = S². Apply this to each arm's fixed potential outcomes. Thus E[V̂N] = S²1/3+S²0/3 = 43/9, exceeding true variance by 2/3.

In the actual sample, treated centre variance is 67/12 and control centre variance is 1, giving V̂N = 79/36. Treating workers as iid instead gives 68/45. Neither expression creates an exact normal interval. More subtly, 79/36 < 37/9: the Neyman estimate is conservative in expectation, not pointwise for every realized assignment. The finite-randomization source distinguishes this design perspective from superpopulation inference.

For the sharp outcome null Wzjr identical for all assignments, keep the actual observed W fixed. For every three-centre set compute its contrast. Four of twenty absolute contrasts are at least |11/3|, giving 1/5. For ANCOVA keep actual W and B fixed but refit 1,Z,b for every assignment: six coefficients have absolute value at least |191/48|, giving 3/10. The two statistics were declared as separate alternatives, not chosen by their resulting p-values. A selection rule would itself have to be replayed for a selection-aware exact test.

Why is this exact? Under the sharp null the full outcome vector is fixed, so the actual assignment is uniform among the twenty reference entries. Sort the absolute statistics from largest to smallest, retaining tied blocks. The inclusive upper-tail rank of an entry equals the cumulative size of its block. The set of entries with p ≤ α contains at most 20α entries, so its probability is at most α. This is a finite counting proof; it does not use a Gaussian approximation, independent worker errors or a probability that the null is true.

4. Invert the adjusted-outcome sharp null — P5 and P6

Under Hτ, Rjr = Wjr(z)−τDjr(z) is invariant across assignments. Its observed value therefore supplies the full fixed residual vector required by the rank argument, even if unobserved receipt decisions are unknown. Under exclusion, Hτ requires the common effect τ among the compliers; A/N can have other receipt effects because their receipt never changes. An average-effect restriction alone does not make the missing residuals known.

aS = contrast of fixed observed W under S; bS = contrast of fixed observed D under S.
p(τ) = (1/20)ΣS1{|aS−bSτ| ≥ |a0−b0τ|}, with (a0,b0) = (11/3,5/6).

Each comparison changes only where [(aS−a0)−(bS−b0)τ][(aS+a0)−(bS+b0)τ] = 0. For a nonzero linear coefficient record its exact rational root. Constant nonzero factors have no root. If a comparison is identically tied, meaning (a,b) = (a₀,b₀) or (−a₀,−b₀), count its tie for every τ but skip it when collecting roots. There are at most forty candidate roots from the remaining comparisons. On each resulting open interval both signs are fixed, so one rational interior point determines the count on the entire interval. Test every boundary separately and both unbounded tails. Merge adjacent accepted cells only when their shared boundary is included. This proves completeness of the algorithm on R.

The baseline distinct roots are 0, 1, 2, 11/4, 3, 13/4, 11/3, 15/4, 13/3, 9/2, 11/2, 6, 13/2, 20/3, 7, 22/3, 9, 11. Exact evaluation of all roots and intervening cells gives p ≤ 1/5 outside [1,9] and p > 1/5 throughout [1,9]. For example p(0) = 1/5, p(1) = 3/10, p(4) = 9/10, p(9) = 3/10 and p(10) = 1/5. Therefore rejection at p ≤ 1/5 leaves [1,9], including both endpoints. The output retains the complete root list and explicit endpoint flags; a finite plotting grid cannot prove the same conclusion.

If a true scalar τ satisfies Hτ, the finite rank proof gives Pr(τ retained) ≥ 1−α. This is coverage for the stated sharp model. Here the six complier effects are (2,4,6,2,4,6), so no common scalar satisfies Hτ. The fact that [1,9] contains their mean 4 establishes no generic LATE coverage. As a separate validation population, set all six complier effects to 4 while preserving types, untreated changes and A/N effects. H4 then holds. Enumeration gives true-null rejection probability 1/5 at α = 1/5, consistent with the bound; this population is not the observed trial.

Every assignment S has a distinct equally likely complement with the opposite residual contrast. Their absolute values tie, so p ≥ 2/20 for every τ, including values with zero actual contrast. At α = 1/20 no τ is rejected: the inversion is all of R, and true-null rejection probability is zero. This coarse resolution is an honest limitation of six centres. It cannot be fixed by declaring twelve independent assignments.

5. Access loss changes both the target and the evidence — extension 1

The new world removes the centre 2 complier with receipt effect 6. The sum of complier effects falls from 24 to 18 and the count from 6 to 5. Hence θZ = 3/2, π = 5/12 and θC = 18/5. This is a new potential population and assignment, not a correction of the original records after seeing results.

Under {1,2,4}, encouraged centre changes are (1,1,−1), with mean 1/3; unencouraged changes are (9/2,9/2,0), with mean 3. The observed difference is -8/3. Each arm has mean receipt 1/3, so the first stage is 0. The ratio is undefined. Return a null value with undefined_zero_first_stage; zero, an infinite coefficient or a narrow normal interval would be false precision.

Regenerating all twenty assignments in this changed world yields three zero first stages. An unconditional expectation of the ratio is not defined on this assignment space. Averaging only the other seventeen observations would condition on a data-dependent event and answer another question; the supplied output therefore reports a null expectation with a support-failure reason.

The sharp adjusted-outcome test itself needs no division by the first stage. Its actual line is a0−b0τ = −8/3. Its distinct crossing roots are −9, −7, −5, 1, 7, 9, 11. Evaluate all cells as before: p > 1/5 for τ ≤ 1 or τ ≥ 7 and p ≤ 1/5 on (1,7). At the boundaries p(1) = 3/10 and p(7) = 2/5; p(4) = 1/5. The complete inversion is (−∞,1] ∪ [7,∞). Unboundedness and disconnection are valid properties of the test, not serialization defects. Its heterogeneous-effect confidence limitation remains unchanged. At α = 1/20 the complement argument again gives all of R.

6. Prove what exclusion cannot be learned from these observables — P7

For a complier, D(z) = z. Substituting into the changed law gives Wδ(D(z),z) = v+(τ−δ)z+δz = v+τz. Thus for every worker, both possible own-centre assignments and every one of the twenty allowed joint assignments, B,D,W,Y are exactly as before. A/N laws are unchanged by construction. The complete observed-data law, not merely one fitted moment, is identical for every δ ∈ [−1,1].

Holding z fixed and intervening on receipt gives Wδ(1,z)−Wδ(0,z) = τ−δ. Averaging among compliers yields θC,δ = 4−δ, so the allowed set is [3,5]. The lower endpoint uses δ = 1, the upper uses δ = −1, and each intermediate target c uses δ = 4−c. That admissible construction attains every point while preserving the entire observable law, proving sharpness. Bounds outside this declared common complier-specific direct-effect class have not been proved.

The invitation ITT remains 2 and the first stage 1/2. Their ratio remains 4, but now equals the receipt effect 4−δ plus the direct invitation contribution δ among receipt-switchers. It cannot isolate training alone. Random assignment protects the invitation comparison from selection; it does not prevent the invitation from changing motivation, information or other outcome determinants. Those channels are substantive identification questions.

7. A defensible referee report and external transfer

An adequate synthetic referee report opens with a conditional conclusion: “The fixed experiment identifies the average effect of encouragement under the stipulated assignment and no-interference contract. The observed change contrast is 11/3, while its finite assignment expectation is 2. Under additional exclusion and monotone receipt, the ratio of finite assignment effects identifies the complier receipt effect 4; the observed ratio 22/5 is neither that exact target nor an unbiased estimator in this small design.” It then documents the receipt-OLS, assignment-unit, sharp-null and exclusion errors, their numerical consequences and the revisions required. It does not infer no effect from p = 1/5 or superiority from one smaller p-value. The ASA interpretation principles support that caution.

The external dossier has no fabricated numerical answer key. Full credit requires evidence appropriate to the selected paper: exact claim/primary location; coherent estimand and counterfactual; assumptions distinguished from diagnostics; actual dependence and selection rules; a reproducible input-to-exhibit map; and a conclusion limited to those facts. In the execution branch, matching one table is a reported computational result, while identification and transport remain separate. In the limitation branch, a specific documented obstacle, truthful “not executed” status and executable-in-principle protocol earn audit credit, never an invented empirical achievement.

For example, a feasible identification extension to an actual invitation study could specify a justified direct-effect sensitivity class, state the additional evidence needed to bound it, and show how the receipt conclusion varies. A feasible inference extension could replay that study's actual clustered or stratified assignment with its prespecified statistic, but only if the design and needed records are available. These are illustrative proposals, not claims that a selected external paper has that design or that its results have been run. The learner must adapt them to inspected evidence rather than copy the Harbor Skills assumptions.

For grading, a correct exact alternative implementation, an independently proved bound or an evidence-supported different research recommendation can earn full credit. A protocol without actual execution must retain that status even with an excellent score. The completed textbook exercise does not itself certify the learner's research, teaching or institutional competence.

Teach-back and a delayed transfer

Teach-back. In three minutes distinguish θZ, θC, the sample Wald ratio and a sharp Hτ. Explain which two numbers are averaged in each ratio and whose randomness defines its uncertainty. Delayed check. Without the guide, restore the original population, use α = 1/20 and set δ = 1/2. State the inversion, the fixed-z complier receipt effect and whether any observed score changes. Then explain why a failed external-data download cannot be logged as successful replication.

Retention answer

The sharp inversion is all of R because its two-sided p-value is at least 1/10. The isolated receipt effect is 4−1/2 = 7/2, while every observed score, receipt and assignment effect is unchanged. The ratio of assignment effects is still 4 and no longer isolates receipt alone. A failed permitted access attempt supports a documented limitation and a proposed protocol; it supplies no executed empirical result. The teach-back must name the assignment-law expectations and distinguish common sharp effects from heterogeneous averages.

Source scope and computational limits

This project reuses the previously inspected Imbens–Angrist binary-compliance scope, Ding's finite complete-randomization variance/rank scope, ASA principles/reporting scope and the official AEA documentation/access scope as read on 9 October 2026, including its February 2026 policy version. Prior actual inspectors are recorded in the source review; this project makes no fresh whole-body reading claim. The AEA material is dated professional context, not universal law or an endorsement. All population data, variants, formulas specialized to this law, proof calculations and research-brief errors are original.

The reference lab supports the supplied fixed six-centre population, all twenty coherent actual assignment tables, α ∈ {1/5,1/20} and the stated direct-effect class. It is not a generic econometrics engine. It rejects unsupported population changes, malformed records and unknown fields. Exact rationals avoid numerical tie ambiguities; explicit null/unbounded flags preserve mathematical meaning. The standard-library code, all input and reference files and full reproduction instructions work offline. Numerical agreement remains one part of substantive review.

Oral defense and fresh transfer

After the written form and project, allow about 30 minutes for five explanations. Each carries four points. The suggested pass is 17/20 with at least three points on each item and no unresolved critical error. This is an authored criterion, not a calibrated professional examination. Before showing the illustrations, have a reviewer ask one unannounced follow-up per item. Change an assumption or input and require a new conclusion, rather than accepting a recitation of the supplied answer. Record the exact follow-up and its assessment. If studying alone, record the explanation before opening the illustration; seek an informed reader for feedback on the research defense.

  1. An instrument's name is not a restriction. A centered population obeys Y=βD+γZ+u, with E[Z²]=1, E[Zu]=0, E[ZD]=2 and E[ZY]=4. Explain what the usual ratio assumes about γ. If only −1≤γ≤1 is known, derive the identified set for β and give two compatible complete data-generating constructions with different β.
  2. A comparison can already be treated. Two equally sized cohorts E and L have observed means at dates 0,1,2 of (0,5,6) and (0,0,2), respectively. E starts treatment at 1 and L at 2. In the stipulated teaching world, every cohort's untreated mean is zero at every date and there is no anticipation. Compute the date-1-to-2 difference-in-differences using E as L's comparison. Compare it with L's true date-2 effect. Explain how an additional never-treated cohort with means (0,0,0) changes the relevant comparison.
  3. A stable relation need not have stable levels. Let X₀=0, Xₜ=Xₜ₋₁+Uₜ, and Yₜ=2Xₜ+Vₜ, where all Uₜ and Vₜ are mutually independent fair signs. Give a stationary linear relation, compute Var(Xₜ), and explain why applying a stationary-level regression theorem without checking its assumptions is unjustified. Does finding this relation establish the causal effect of intervening on X?
  4. A sufficient rate condition is not a verdict. For an orthogonal cross-fitted score, suppose both nuisance L² errors are Oₚ(n−1/5). The available remainder bound is a constant times their product, with uniform overlap and bounded outcomes. Evaluate its root-n order. Does this prove that the estimator cannot be asymptotically normal? State one concrete rate improvement that makes this product remainder negligible, and identify other conditions still needed.
  5. Reproduce the claim as well as the number. A report says “the randomized invitation increased treatment receipt's effect by four.” Two scripts both return four and have recorded hashes. One computes the difference in outcomes by invitation, the other by actual receipt; no output labels or assignment log were retained. Explain why agreement does not resolve the report. Specify the minimum next evidence you would request and the wording you could currently defend.
Oral illustrations and four-point rubrics
  1. Multiplying by Z and taking expectations gives 4=2β+γ. The usual ratio 4/2=2 assumes the exclusion γ=0 in addition to the stated moment restriction. The sensitivity set is β=2−γ/2, hence [3/2,5/2]. For complete witnesses let Z be a fair sign, D=2Z, Y=4Z and u=0. Both (β,γ)=(3/2,1) and (5/2,−1), and every intervening pair, generate exactly those same observed variables. The set is sharp under the allowed model and is not a sampling confidence interval. Credit: moment equation/exclusion 1; set 1; complete witnesses 1; identification-versus-uncertainty distinction 1. Follow-up: a narrower admissible direct effect should narrow the set through the same equation.
  2. The late cohort's change is two; the already-treated cohort's change is one. The comparison therefore returns 1, although L's date-2 treatment effect is 2. The omitted one is E's treatment-effect growth from five to six. With the never-treated cohort, L's change relative to its zero change is two, justified by the explicitly stipulated untreated trends and no anticipation. The arithmetic does not establish those conditions in an observed study. Credit: comparison 1; true effect 1; contamination mechanism 1; valid alternative and its assumption 1. Follow-up: change E's date-2 effect to five and explain why this particular contaminated comparison then happens to recover two.
  3. Yₜ−2Xₜ=Vₜ is iid with mean zero and variance one, while Var(Xₜ)=t. The levels lack a time-invariant finite variance, so a covariance-stationary-level theorem cannot be invoked. Cointegration concerns a stable stochastic relation among nonstationary series; its estimation and inference require a suitable nonstationary theory. The construction supplies no independent policy-intervention contract: an intervention might change the relation itself or other structural channels. Credit: relation 1; level variance 1; theorem scope 1; causal boundary 1. Follow-up: replacing 2 by a known alternative coefficient in the law changes the stationary relation, not the need to check level behavior.
  4. The available product bound is Oₚ(n−2/5), whose root-n order is Oₚ(n^(1/10)). This bound does not guarantee an oₚ(1) root-n remainder. It does not prove that the actual remainder grows or that normality fails: the bound may be loose or the bias terms may cancel. Improving one nuisance to Oₚ(n−1/2) while retaining Oₚ(n−1/5) for the other gives root-n product Oₚ(n−1/5)=oₚ(1). One still needs an appropriate independent sampling unit, fixed or otherwise controlled folds, held-out evaluation, nuisance L² convergence, common overlap, integrability and a nondegenerate oracle variance with valid estimation. Credit: product and scaling 1; sufficient-condition logic 1; valid improvement 1; remaining conditions 1.
  5. Invitation and receipt index different comparisons. The randomized invitation contrast can target an intention-to-treat effect under the actual assignment contract; the receipt contrast can retain selection. Their numerical equality may be accidental. Request the unit and assignment mechanism/log, versioned inputs and transforms, the two exact estimators and denominators, noncompliance information, outcome/missingness definitions, and the assumptions connecting receipt to outcomes. To turn a randomized invitation into a receipt-effect claim requires further conditions such as relevance, exclusion and the relevant compliance restriction, with the corresponding target stated. Presently one can say only that two retained programs returned four on unspecified analysis inputs; neither a reproducible estimate with verified inputs nor the quoted causal interpretation has been established. Credit: target distinction 1; concrete evidence 1; receipt-identification restrictions 1; defensible wording 1.

Delayed retention assessment

After two to four weeks without rereading these solutions, attempt the five new problems. Allow approximately 120 minutes with a basic calculator and no notes; this timing is uncalibrated. Each problem carries ten points. The proposed threshold is 43/50 overall, at least eight on each item, and correction of every critical error. These compact transfers do not replace the full written form or project. If a score falls short, reconstruct the relevant chapter argument and then solve a fresh problem with altered inputs.

  1. Two moments, one parameter. A correctly specified scalar model has population moment vector a−Bβ, with a=(2,6)′ and B=(1,3)′. Assume the stated iid regularity gives a centered root-n sample-moment normal limit at the true parameter, with covariance Ω=[(2,1);(1,4)]. For identity-weight GMM find β, the row K mapping the moment fluctuation into the parameter fluctuation, and its limiting variance KΩK′. Find the efficient row and variance. Prove that this efficient row minimizes variance among all rows L satisfying LB=1. State why the calculation alone does not establish validity of proposed empirical moments.
  2. Random assignment with missing outcomes. An iid population has potential binary outcomes Y(1),Y(0), potential response indicators R(1),R(0), and a fair assignment Z independent of their whole joint law. Only R=R(Z) and the responding outcome are observed. In both arms the response probability is 3/4; respondent outcome means are 2/3 in arm 1 and 1/3 in arm 0. No other restriction connects response and outcome. Derive the sharp population ATE bounds and the complete-case contrast. Construct full potential-variable laws attaining the endpoints. Then impose the additional information E[Y(1)|R(1)=0]∈[1/5,2/5] and E[Y(0)|R(0)=0]∈[3/5,4/5]; derive the new sharp bounds. Distinguish these bounds from a confidence interval.
  3. Negative serial correlation. For all integer t let εₜ be iid N(0,9), and define Yₜ=μ+εₜ−εₜ₋₁/3. Derive the lag-zero and lag-one autocovariances, all later autocovariances and the long-run variance. Find the exact variance and distribution of the five-observation sample mean, and compare with an independence calculation. Give an exact central 95% interval for μ using the standard-normal 0.975 quantile z₀.₉₇₅. In a separate forecasting exercise with known μ=0 and observed innovation state ε₅=3, find the conditional mean and variance of Y₆ given the innovations through date 5.
  4. Scaling a penalty and updating a prior. For a fixed centered design, X′X/n=I₂ and X′y/n=(2,−1/2)′. Minimize ‖y−Xb‖²/(2n)+(3/4)(|b₁|+|b₂|), and verify the active and inactive KKT conditions. Replace the first design column by 2X₁, retaining the same unweighted coefficient penalty. Find the new first coefficient and its contribution expressed as a coefficient on the original X₁. What penalty weight restores the old fitted contribution? Separately, θ is zero or one with prior P(θ=1)=1/4. A binary observation has P(Y=1|θ=0)=1/4 and P(Y=1|θ=1)=3/4. After observing Y=1, compute the posterior probability of θ=1 and state its evidential scope.
  5. Selection and transport are different operations. Under a global null, two prespecified p-values are independent U(0,1), and a report releases only their minimum M. Derive P(M≤u), a valid continuous selection-adjusted p-value as a function of M, and its value when M=0.04. Would that value reject at 0.05? Separately, a source population has covariate-stratum weights (3/4,1/4) and known stratum treatment effects (−2,4). Under conditional effect transport, a target has weights (1/3,2/3). Calculate both average effects. If only the target stratum-1 weight w∈[2/5,4/5] is known, derive the sharp target-effect set. State what must be retained to audit each calculation.
Retention solutions and ten-point scoring
  1. The unique compatible coefficient is β=2. Identity weighting gives K=(B′B)−1B′=(1,3)/10 and variance (2+6+36)/100=11/25. Since Ω−1=(1/7)[(4,−1);(−1,2)], Ω−1B=(1,5)′/7 and B′Ω−1B=16/7. Thus K*=(1,5)/16 and V*=7/16. Ω is positive definite because its leading entry and determinant, two and seven, are positive. For any LB=1, write L=K*+H, so HB=0. K*Ω=B′/(B′Ω−1B), whence K*ΩH′=0. Therefore LΩL′=V*+HΩH′≥V*, with equality only for H=0. The given asymptotic and validity assumptions are inputs; no fit criterion proves exclusion or removes confounding. Credit: target and K 2; identity variance 2; efficient row/variance 2; covariance decomposition and equality 3; validity boundary 1.
  2. Let a and b denote the two missing-outcome means. Then μ₁=(3/4)(2/3)+(1/4)a=1/2+a/4 and μ₀=(3/4)(1/3)+(1/4)b=1/4+b/4. The ATE is 1/4+(a−b)/4, with sharp set [0,1/2]. The complete-case contrast is 1/3. For each potential arm separately, draw R(d) with probability 3/4; conditional on responding, draw Y(d) Bernoulli with the stated respondent mean, and otherwise Bernoulli with mean a or b. Take the two arm-specific pairs independent, then assign Z independently. Setting (a,b)=(0,1) or (1,0) attains the two endpoints while preserving every observed probability. Intermediate choices fill the interval. Under the additional restrictions, a−b∈[−3/5,−1/5], giving [1/10,1/5]; endpoint conditional means within their allowed ranges give the same constructive proof of sharpness. These are population identification sets conditional on supplied exact probabilities and assumptions. Finite-sample uncertainty about those probabilities would require another layer of inference. Credit: mean equations and original set 3; complete-case contrast 1; full compatible constructions and sharpness 3; refined set 2; uncertainty distinction 1.
  3. The variance is γ₀=9+9/9=10. The single shared innovation at lag one has coefficient product −1/3, so γ₁=−3; later covariances vanish. The long-run variance is 4. For five observations, Var(Ȳ₅)=[5(10)+2(4)(−3)]/25=26/25, whereas independence would give 10/5=2. Gaussian linear combinations imply Ȳ₅∼N(μ,26/25) exactly. Hence [Ȳ₅−z₀.₉₇₅√26/5,Ȳ₅+z₀.₉₇₅√26/5] has exact 95% coverage under this known-covariance law. In the separate known-μ forecasting exercise, Y₆=ε₆−1 conditionally, with mean −1 and variance 9. The unconditional mean-interval calculation has not been conditioned on a subsequently fixed innovation. Credit: covariance sequence 2; long-run variance 1; exact finite mean variance and false alternative 3; exact Gaussian interval and scope 2; conditional forecast 2.
  4. Apart from a constant the original criterion is (1/2)Σⱼ(bⱼ−zⱼ)²+(3/4)Σⱼ|bⱼ|. Soft thresholding gives (5/4,0). The first residual correlation is 2−5/4=3/4 with the positive coefficient's sign; the second is −1/2, within [−3/4,3/4], so the zero coordinate satisfies the subgradient condition. The strictly convex quadratic makes the solution unique. Writing c for the coefficient of the doubled column, its positive-coordinate derivative is 4c−4+3/4, so c=13/16; its contribution on original X₁ is 13/8. Penalizing 2|c| instead of |c|, with the same factor 3/4, restores c=5/8 and original contribution 5/4. Coefficient scale changes the meaning of an unadjusted penalty. For the separate Bayesian problem the joint mass at (θ=1,Y=1) is 3/16, equal to that at (θ=0,Y=1), giving posterior 1/2. This is conditional on the declared prior and likelihood; it is not automatically a frequentist coverage or causal claim. Credit: original solution and both KKT conditions 3; scaled solution/contribution 3; restoring penalty 2; posterior and scope 2.
  5. Independence gives FM(u)=1−(1−u)²=2u−u² on [0,1]. This CDF is continuous and strictly increasing, so FM(M) is exactly uniform under the stated global null: for 0≤q≤1 its lower-tail event is M≤1−√(1−q), which has probability q. The adjusted value at 0.04 is 49/625=0.0784, so it does not reject at 0.05. This exact adjustment depends on the supplied independence law and the complete two-test selection rule. The source effect is (3/4)(−2)+(1/4)4=−1/2; the target effect is (1/3)(−2)+(2/3)4=2. With unknown w the target effect is −2+6w, giving [2/5,14/5]. Every w in the allowed range defines a compatible target population, so the set is sharp under conditional effect transport and support. Retain the original testing family, joint-null assumptions and selection rule; separately retain stratum definitions, target weights, effect estimates or stipulated effects, and the justification for transport. Selection adjustment cannot supply transport evidence. Credit: minimum CDF and uniform transformation proof 3; numerical adjusted value/decision 1; source and target effects 2; sharp target set and assumptions 3; distinct audit records 1.

Remediation and advancement record

For each error, record the exact claim, the failed assumption or calculation, the corrected argument and a new transfer. Repeating the same numerical example after seeing its solution does not establish transfer. Diagnose separately an algebra error, a missing probability law, a wrong estimand, a theorem used outside its conditions, and a claim exceeding the available evidence. Reattempt the relevant chapter exercises before the reassessment form.

Observed difficultyReturn toRequired repair evidence
Conditioning, units or missing values in the diagnosticVolumes 2–4; diagnostic solution linksA new exact conditional calculation or compatible completion, with units and the repeated observation specified.
D1: identified target, regularity or covariance1, 2, 3, 4, 5Write the population moment, prove or refute uniqueness, derive an expansion and calculate its covariance from the actual independent unit.
D2: invalid comparison, timing, compliance or support6, 7, 8Supply the potential-outcome or counterfactual law, an identifying argument and a compatible counterexample when one assumption is removed.
D3: persistence, simulation or policy extrapolation9, 10Reconstruct innovation dependence or simulated moments, then show which primitive or counterfactual remains identified under observational equivalence.
D4: posterior, penalty, nuisance or selection error11Recompute a posterior or KKT system, or derive the score remainder and the complete evaluation/testing rule.
D5: irreproducible or overstated research claim12 and the projectProduce a versioned input-to-output trail, distinguish access from validity, and rewrite the claim to match its target and uncertainty.

Retain the diagnostic score, each written domain score, project rubric, oral follow-ups, delayed scores and dates, plus all critical-error resolutions. Advancement requires the stated written standard, a satisfactory project and oral transfer, and completed remediation. Delayed assessment provides another check of retention; it does not retroactively turn an unresolved identification error into an acceptable result. Research quality still requires informed external evaluation of the learner's actual work.

Notation and concept index

Symbols are local to a model. In particular, n can count persons, independent panels or clusters; an estimator's variance changes with that choice. Keep an estimand's population and weighting rule beside its notation.

Synthesis and the next stage

An econometric argument begins with a question about a population or intervention. Identification determines what the observable law can settle under explicit restrictions. Estimation computes an answer from a finite sample; inference describes uncertainty under a specified repetition or assignment law. Design, dependence, support, missingness and analysis choices affect these stages differently. The most useful conclusion can be an estimate, a bound, a sensitivity relation or a precise statement of what the available evidence cannot distinguish.

The graduate theory volume asks which preferences, technologies, information and equilibrium restrictions support an economic mechanism. Graduate macroeconomics and macro-finance connect such mechanisms to dynamic aggregate evidence. Use the distinction between observable fit and invariant primitives throughout those volumes. The later graduate qualifying sequence integrates econometrics, microeconomic theory and macro-finance; it remains a separate assessment whose availability is shown in the assessment standard and curriculum.

A finished project should let another reader reconstruct both the outputs and the limits of the claim. The external-paper transfer asks the learner to apply that discipline to real research with real access constraints. This library supplies instruction, original problems and evaluation protocols. Original contribution, research judgment and successful supervision require the learner's work and appropriate independent feedback.

Evidence and source scope

The diagnostic, oral illustrations and retention problems are original probability laws, algebraic constructions and audit scenarios. They introduce no measured October 2026 data, current institutional policy or claim about an actual empirical paper. Their methods are taught and sourced in the linked prerequisite and volume chapters. Reusing those verified chapter references does not constitute a new inspection of every source body. The examination and project components state any additional source use and its limits. A deterministic result or matching hash establishes a relation to specified bytes and instructions; scientific validity additionally depends on the meaning and justification of the model and data.
